scenario: Warm vanilla scoreboard baseline
oracle: Reproducible throughput and profile baseline
status: Partial: Partial: the pre-declared baseline campaign was built (scripts/run_perf_001_baseline.py) and run three times, each seven fresh boots of the pinned, hash-verified official 26.3 server over the fixed 5,000-line `function_compiler_perf:scoreboard` fixture with every run's final score verified (5,000 * (warmup + measured)); the gate was pre-declared as a run-median coefficient of variation <= 5% and all three campaigns failed it on this host. Attempt 1 (50 warmup / 300 measured calls) recorded run medians 1.91, 1.15, 1.17, 1.14, 1.32, 2.48 and 2.79 ms (CV 0.375) while the host load rose 6.4 -> 12.5. Attempt 2 (same constants) recorded 1.28, 2.89, 1.86, 1.57, 1.40, 1.64, 1.88 ms (CV 0.276) with load 5.4 -> 14.3. Attempt 3 (350 warmup / 1000 measured calls, declared from the diagnosed variance source - only 50 warmup calls leaves a fresh server's JIT far from tiered-compilation steady state) recorded 0.89, 0.99, 1.97, 1.36, 1.09, 3.48, 1.46 ms with a declared-rerun noisy run at 1.57 ms (CV 0.275) and load 6.2 -> 16.6. The pre-declared design treats a gate failure as recorded data and the campaign now exits nonzero on it. Diagnosis recorded: the host's load climbs during any sustained campaign on this machine and the run medians do not track the load cleanly, so the between-run variance is not purely contention; the metric is the RCON round trip, not execution-only time. The exploratory JFR and local Spark captures and the attempt-7 win remain as recorded. Next action: rerun the same pre-declared campaign on an idle host (or under a tighter pre-declared load precondition, e.g. 1-minute load <= 4), or replace the round-trip metric with an execution-adjacent measurement; the 5.25-million-update verified fixture stays the workload.

scenario: Compilation amortization for cold and hot functions
oracle: Break-even threshold and opt-out policy
status: Verified amortization model and opt-out policy using PERF-004 and PERF-008 data. Emitting hidden JVM classes adds ~19.67 µs per region (1,077 B/class, 2.03 KiB Metaspace). Hot functions amortize on the very first invocation (N* = 1; 610 µs bytecode saving vs 19.67 µs compilation latency). Fused interpretation amortizes on call 1 (963 µs saving vs 119.8 µs latency) with 0 B bytecode/Metaspace overhead. Established four-part cold-function opt-out policy: minimum length threshold (L >= 3), #minecraft:load bypass, deferred JIT compilation threshold (K >= 5), and weak class retention with GC unlinking. See benchmarks/PERF-009-compilation-amortization.md.

The counter half runs in the five Fabric arms where the measurement is live (score-add-on, instrument-only, score-add-timed, fused-interpreted, bytecode-emitted): each reports control_compiled=4, so the measurement is demonstrably capable of reading a nonzero specialization count, and each reports zero for both declined fixtures in both the compiled and executed directions. wrapper-off and wrapper-on compile nothing, so they are recorded as not exercising the contract rather than as passing it. Adds fixtures score_delegation_positive (control), score_selector_declined and state_machine_client_packet, per-function specialization counters on the status command, and tests/test_delegation_contract_fixtures.py. This case is a delegation contract, not a differential parity test: title, playsound, particle and stopsound produce client packets only, which RCON cannot observe, so no parity oracle exists for their effects. What is claimed is that the families are not specialized (structural, zero counters) and are forwarded to vanilla without error (behavioural).
